Commander,

There have been some troubling reports of titan organs being smuggled out of Bava Nisos, and gods only know what people are doing with them. To make matters worse, everyone on location here is either Tyrian Alliance or Astral Ward. Between the two, I've got enough red tape to strangle a damned titan. I can't exactly go kicking doors in without probable cause. Looks like I'm gonna need your help.

Magnus laughed me out of his office when I told him Evon's vaults were broken into by, I kid you not, a cat. Hell, after something like that, nothing's out of the question anymore.

Come find me near the field hospital the ward set up. I'll fill you in on what I know. And look, I know you're plenty busy, but if we let this type of stuff slide, who's to say it won't cause bigger trouble down the road.

Doyen Sidony,  

I have no excuse for my candor in the diplomatic forums; I made a scene in front of you and your assembly, and in the olden memory of Gruna, your trusted friend, you deserved better than the grievances I heaped on you.  

I couldn't stomach the clan council's decision to heed your advice. Shrewd as it was, honorable it was not. Yes, some of the Forgotten ignored my ancestor's advice to avoid settling near the wellspring on the peninsula, but even then, their continued survival would have been preferrable. We are but prey to the dragons, and we should've put the fear of death in them when we had the chance. That is my belief, and I'll not shy away from it.  

That said, I've not the right or rank to offer support against the mursaat on behalf of my people. The council has been in tatters after the fire wyrm burrowed throughout the depths over the passing years. We are disorganized, digging through the rubble of the old world with nary a hint as to where the beast took to. Some clans sat pretty atop deep wells of ley magic, and they paid the steepest price despite Clan Way's warnings. Their townships have gone dark and silent. For now, many of the old routes, paths through the depths, are greatly changed or cut off for us.  

It's not what you wanted to hear, but it's the truth. We'll be lucky if the mursaat don't turn their spiteful gaze on us in time. We fell to your side, after all.  

My regrets,  
—Boward Waylit
